expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response addresses the three decisive questions clearly: (1) Is quality measured at all? Yes, one job exists (llmops-demo-eval), but it evaluated the wrong model (Nova-lite, not the production Sonnet-5 model carrying 97% of traffic) - this is a nuanced and more accurate finding than a simple yes/no, correctly noting LLM-EVAL-001 is "Not raised" since a job does exist. (2) Is it measured automatically/wired into CI/CD? The agent explicitly addresses this - LLM-EVAL-002 is flagged HIGH severity, noting only one job ran ~40 days ago and "CI/CD can't be confirmed from AWS APIs," inferring it's likely manual. (3) Can a regression reach production? LLM-EVAL-007 (no regression gate) is flagged HIGH, explicitly stating "No gate evidence is visible through AWS APIs."

The response doesn't explicitly state upfront "us-east-1 supports Bedrock evaluation" as a standalone confirmation, but it implicitly confirms this by describing an actual evaluation job that ran in the region (llmops-demo-eval), which demonstrates regional support without needing to state it separately. Since a job list is non-empty, the CRITICAL-vs-INFO distinction for empty job lists doesn't directly apply, but the agent correctly treats the existing job as evidence the capability works, and appropriately escalates severity on the automation and regression-gate gaps instead.

The findings table format with severity levels (HIGH, MEDIUM, OK, Not raised) also aligns well with the expected structured reporting of evaluation health. Overall, the three decisive questions are substantively and correctly answered, satisfying the core intent of the expected output even though the exact framing (regional support confirmation first, empty-list interpretation) isn't verbatim present given the job list wasn't empty.
